He expanded through post-war ship purchases and new vessels commissioned from Japanese yards, creating an international network of offices.

long_biography.plain_text:
When shipowner Evangelos Nomikos and his wife, Loula, offered to fund a major project on Santorini, local authorities chose a hotel over a hospital. The couple commissioned the Atlantis, which survived the island's destructive 1956 earthquake and temporarily served as a hospital and public-service building.

Nomikos also tackled the difficult journey between the old port and Fira. He paid for the purchase and installation of a cable car through the foundation he established in 1979. Its income supported community development, with part of ticket receipts also allocated to the mule drivers whose livelihoods were affected by the new transport link.

confidence.reason: Hotel's own history, foundation's explanation and published founder memorial support the separate hospitality and transport contributions. Later foundation air-ambulance work is not attributed to him.
